key_insight: Physics-constrained causal discovery can identify constitutive mechanism dependencies from full-field displacements, while correlated observational data can conceal the correct graph.
engineering_relevance: Controlled climate interventions can improve constitutive-model reliability under unseen conditions without requiring stress or internal-variable measurements.
method: Embed balance laws and constitutive skeletons in time-unrolled causal models scored by weak-form equilibrium gaps.
Use adaptive lasso and a NOTEARS-type acyclicity constraint to select mechanism dependencies.
Use an autodifferentiated Gauss–Newton matrix to assess local identifiability and guide greedy D-optimal test design.
evidence_signal: In a synthetic plate study with 0.01-pixel displacement noise, interventional data recovered the exact 8-edge graph in 7/10 runs and kept prediction errors within 3.2%, versus up to 41.5% for observationally discovered models.
watch_item: Evidence is synthetic, and noise bias in the weak-form score remains a primary limitation.
paper_title: Physics-constrained differentiable causal discovery of constitutive mechanisms through boundary value problems
